mishnah_berurah.he:
(י) אסור להשכיר וכו' - אפילו ביום ראשון ואפילו בהבלעה:
(יא) כדי שיעשה וכו' - צ"ל שמא יעשה בה [הגר"א וכן מוכח מהש"ע גופא]:
(יב) על שביתת בהמתו - דכתיב למען ינוח שורך וחמורך וגו' ואע"ג דהשכיר הבהמה לא"י הא קי"ל דשכירות לא קניא והו"ל בהמתו של ישראל ומצווה על שביתתה וי"א דלחומרא אמרינן דשכירות קניא וע"כ אם ישראל שכר בהמה מא"י מצווה על שביתתה ונכון להחמיר כיון דהוא איסור דאורייתא ואם שכרה מא"י וחזר והשכירה לא"י שרי ממה נפשך. ואם קנה בהמה מא"י או מכר לא"י במשיכה לחוד או בכסף לחוד הוי ספיקא דדינא ואזלינן לחומרא לענין שביתת בהמה [תו"ש]:
(יג) אין הא"י נאמן - ומירתת נמי לא מירתת לעשות בה מלאכה כיון שהוא ברשותו ע"י שאלה או שכירות לא נתפס עליו כגנב עי"ז משא"כ ברישא כשמתנה שיחזירנה לו קודם שבת כבר כלה השאלה והשכירות קודם השבת ועי' לקמן סי' ש"ה סכ"ג [אחרונים]:
(יד) יפקירנה וכו' - וזהו דוקא בדיעבד שכבר התנה עמו ועיכבה בשבת אבל לכתחלה אסור להשכירה ע"ד שכשיגיע יום השבת שיפקירנה ואפילו אם יפקירנה בפני שלשה שאין הכל יודעים מן ההפקר ואתי לידי חשדא שיאמרו בהמתו של ישראל עושה מלאכה בשבת ואף במכירה אין היתר אלא כשמוכר בהמתו לא"י במכירה גמורה על כל ימי השבוע ולא כשמוכר לו על יום השבת לחוד מפני חשדא וכנ"ל והב"ח מתיר לכתחלה להשכיר ע"ד שיפקירנה בפני ג' דכיון דג' ליודעים מיפרסמא מילתא ולא יבא לידי חשדא ובשעת הדחק אפשר שיש לסמוך על דבריו ובסוף הסימן נבאר אי"ה:
(טו) בינו לבין עצמו - שאז אינו מצווה על שביתתה כיון שאינו שלו שכבר הפקירה ואע"ג דהפקר בעינן שיהיה בפני שלשה זהו מדרבנן אבל מדאורייתא אפילו בינו לבין עצמו סגי והכא שכבר השכירה והתנה עמו שיחזירנה ועיכבה די בזה כדי להנצל מאיסורא דאורייתא ועיין בב"י שיש פוסקים שסוברין דגם בכאן אף שהוא דיעבד בעינן דוקא תלתא וע"כ טוב ליזהר בזה לכתחלה אם יש באפשרי ועכ"פ יזהר להפקירה בפני אחד דרבים מגדולי הפוסקים סוברים דאף דאורייתא אינה הפקר עד שיפקירה עכ"פ בפני אדם אחד ואפילו בפני אחד מאנשי ביתו די בזה:
(טז) בהמתו קנויה להא"י - עיין במ"א שדעתו דדוקא אם אומר לו בפניו בהמתי קנויה לך שאז מתכוין הא"י לקנותה והיא נקנית לו באמירה זו כיון שהיא ברשותו וקניא ליה חצירו אבל אם אומר כן שלא בפניו לא קנאה הא"י כלל. ואפילו אם זיכה לו ע"י ישראל אחר ג"כ לא מהני כמבואר בח"מ סימן רמ"ג סי"ד וכן הסכים הפמ"ג ושארי אחרונים כהמ"א ופשוט דאפילו באומר בהמתי קנויה לך בעינן שיהיה לזה ג"כ פסיקת דמים דאל"ה אין זה מכירה כלל וכ"כ בח"א בכלל נ"ח:
(יז) כדי שינצל וכו' - ר"ל אבל לכתחלה אין לסמוך להשכיר ע"ד שיפקיר כשיגיע יום השבת או שיקנהו אז להא"י שההפקר וההקנאה אינן מפורסמין ויש כאן חשש מראית העין וכנ"ל ועין בסוף הסימן:
(יח) דודאי אין כונתו - ר"ל שבודאי לא היה בדעתו שישאר הפקר לעולם כ"א ליום השבת בלבד כדי להפקיע מעליו איסור שבת ולאחר השבת יחזור לרשותו אבל ביום השבת גופא בודאי הוא הפקר גמור [וגם זה מקרי בשם הפקר וכדאיתא בגמרא דאפילו הפקר ליום אחד הוי הפקר] ואין צריך לחוש שמא יזכה בה אחר בשבת גופא שבודאי הא"י לא יניחנו כ"ז שהיא ת"י למלאכתו:
(יט) אין אדם מצווה וכו' - דשביתת בהמתו ילפינן ממה דכתיב למען ינוח שורך וחמורך כמוך והאי קרא בשבת כתיב ואפ"ה לא ישכירם אלא בהבלעה דלא יהיה שכר יו"ט והנה המהרש"ל חולק ע"ז ודעתו דיו"ט ושבת שוין הן בזה כמו בכל מלאכות ועין במג"א שהאריך בזה ומביא דהב"י בסימן תצ"ה הביא דעות הראשונים בזה ומצדד שם לאיסור וע"כ יש להחמיר ובביאור הגר"א ג"כ האריך בזה ומסיק דהעיקר כדעת מהרש"ל הנ"ל וגם לקמן בסימן תצ"ה ס"ג מפרש הגר"א מה שכתוב שם בשו"ע דאין מוציאין משא על הבהמה ביו"ט הטעם הוא משום שביתת בהמתו:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(10) It is forbidden to rent out, etc. - Even on the first day of the week, and even by inclusion.
(11) In order that it do, etc. - It should read: lest he do with it, as Gra writes, and so is proven from the Shulchan Aruch itself.
(12) Regarding the resting of his animal - For it is written, "so that your ox and your donkey may rest," etc. Although he rented the animal to a non-Jew, we hold that rental does not acquire, so it remains the animal of the Jew and he is commanded regarding its rest. Some say that stringently we say rental does acquire; therefore, if a Jew rented an animal from a non-Jew, he is commanded regarding its rest. It is proper to be stringent, since this is a Torah prohibition. If he rented it from a non-Jew and then rented it back to a non-Jew, it is permitted whichever way one looks at it. If he bought an animal from a non-Jew or sold it to a non-Jew with meshikhah alone or money alone, this is a doubtful law, and we follow stringency regarding the resting of an animal, as Tosefet Shabbat writes.
(13) The non-Jew is not believed - Nor is he afraid to do labor with it, since it is in his possession by borrowing or rental, and he will not be caught as a thief because of this. This is unlike the first case, where he stipulates that he return it before Shabbat, for the borrowing or rental has already ended before Shabbat. See below siman 305 seif 23, as the Acharonim write.
(14) He should declare it ownerless, etc. - This is specifically after the fact, where he already stipulated with him and the non-Jew detained it on Shabbat. But initially it is forbidden to rent it with the intention that when Shabbat arrives he will declare it ownerless; even if he declares it ownerless before three people, not everyone knows of the hefker, and it may lead to suspicion, for people will say that a Jew's animal is doing labor on Shabbat. Even with a sale, there is no permission except when he sells his animal to the non-Jew as a complete sale for all the days of the week, not when he sells it to him for Shabbat alone, because of suspicion, as above. Bach permits initially to rent it on the condition that he will declare it ownerless before three people, for since three know, the matter becomes public and will not lead to suspicion. In pressing circumstances perhaps one may rely on his words. At the end of the siman we will explain, God willing.
(15) Between himself and himself - Then he is not commanded regarding its rest, since it is not his, for he already declared it ownerless. Although hefker requires being before three people, that is rabbinic; but by Torah law even between himself and himself suffices. Here, where he already rented it and stipulated with him that he return it, and the non-Jew detained it, this is enough to be saved from a Torah prohibition. See Beit Yosef, for there are poskim who hold that even here, although it is after the fact, specifically three are required. Therefore it is good to be careful about this initially if possible. In any case, he should be careful to declare it ownerless before one person, for many of the great poskim hold that even by Torah law it is not hefker until he declares it ownerless at least before one person, and even one of his household suffices.
(16) His animal is acquired by the non-Jew - See Magen Avraham, whose view is that this is specifically if he says to him in his presence, "My animal is acquired by you," for then the non-Jew intends to acquire it and it is acquired to him by this statement, since it is in his possession and his courtyard acquires for him. But if he says this not in his presence, the non-Jew does not acquire it at all. Even if he transfers it to him through another Jew, this also does not help, as explained in Choshen Mishpat siman 243 seif 14. Peri Megadim and the other Acharonim agreed with Magen Avraham. It is obvious that even when he says, "My animal is acquired by you," there must also be a fixed price for it, for otherwise it is not a sale at all; so wrote Chayei Adam, klal 58.
(17) So that he be saved, etc. - Meaning, initially one should not rely on renting with the intention that he will declare it ownerless when Shabbat arrives, or that he will then transfer ownership to the non-Jew, for the hefker and transfer are not publicized, and there is concern for marit ayin, as above. See the end of the siman.
(18) For certainly his intention is not - Meaning, certainly he did not intend that it remain ownerless forever, but only for Shabbat, in order to remove from himself the Shabbat prohibition; after Shabbat it will return to his domain. But on Shabbat itself it is certainly complete hefker. This too is called hefker, as stated in the Gemara, that even hefker for one day is hefker. One need not be concerned that another will acquire it on Shabbat itself, for the non-Jew will certainly not allow that as long as it is in his hand for his labor.
(19) A person is not commanded, etc. - For the resting of one's animal is learned from the verse "so that your ox and your donkey may rest like you," and that verse is written regarding Shabbat. Nevertheless, he should rent them only by inclusion, so there not be payment for Yom Tov. Maharshal disagrees with this, and his view is that Yom Tov and Shabbat are equal in this matter, as in all labors. See Magen Avraham, who discusses this at length and brings that Beit Yosef in siman 495 cited the views of the Rishonim about this and inclines there to prohibit. Therefore one should be stringent. In Biur HaGra he also discusses this at length and concludes that the essential law is like Maharshal. Also below in siman 495 seif 3, Gra explains that what is written there in Shulchan Aruch, that one may not carry a load on an animal on Yom Tov, is because of the resting of one's animal.

mechaber.en: If a Jew and a Non-Jew are partners in an animal, the Non-Jew may use it for work on Shabbat if it was established with the non-Jew at the beginning, when it was bought, that the non-Jew will assume control of it on Shabbat and the Jew will have control of it during the weekdays. If they did not stipulate to this at the beginning, it is forbidden, even though they may have stipulated to this afterwards....

yad_ephraim.en: And what Magen Avraham wrote, and these are his words: and what the Yerushalmi wrote — we do not ride because of shvisas beheimah; behold a living being carries itself, etc. And seemingly, per what he wrote that shvisah does not apply to hotzaah at all and a person is also permitted — if so, without this that a living being carries itself, one should have asked that even if the rider is like a load it is also permitted on Yom Tov; and it is strained to say that he preferred this and cited that even on Shabbat there is no prohibition of a living being carrying itself, as the Bach's difficulty in siman 305 — this is strained; and thus I heard they ask in the name of the eminent rabbi R' Naftali son of R' Levi z"l. And further — how is this difficulty connected to rejecting the proof from what was written above? And in my humble opinion the intent of Magen Avraham is because one can say in the intent of the Bach that seemingly the Bach properly brought proof from what he wrote that one is not commanded regarding shvisas beheimah on Yom Tov, and there is no rejection that there it deals with hotzaah and hotzaah was also permitted for a person, etc. — for in truth this is what he said: for the Bach challenged the Yerushalmi (per the Bach's words, the Yerushalmi's words actually refer to Shabbat) that behold a living being carries itself, and he needed to answer that even though one is not commanded regarding riding it on an animal, nevertheless since the animal suffers in his riding upon it he violates shvisas beheimah — see in the Bach. And accordingly, if we say that on Yom Tov also the positive commandment of shvisas beheimah applies — what of it that hotzaah is permitted on Yom Tov? Nevertheless it is forbidden to ride on it and to take out loads, since it has pain in riding and taking out loads is included in shvisas beheimah; rather one must say that Shulchan Aruch holds that on Yom Tov the positive commandment of shvisas beheimah does not apply at all, and this Yerushalmi teaches regarding Shabbat; and thus Magen Avraham wrote that the Bach's difficulties on the Yerushalmi regarding a living being carrying itself are not difficult for us, and the continuation of Magen Avraham's words is thus: that Yeshuos Yaakov brings proof from the plain meaning of the Yerushalmi's words — it appears that regarding Yom Tov it teaches; and on this Magen Avraham wrote; and see Bach siman 305 — meaning that there the Bach brought the Yerushalmi's words regarding Shabbat because he proved from what was written above that there is no shvisas beheimah on Yom Tov, and therefore he established it regarding Shabbat; and therefore Magen Avraham wrote that from Shulchan Aruch's words there is no proof, for there it deals with hotzaah, and in any case for other hotzaah the positive commandment of shvisas beheimah applies on Yom Tov; and that which the Yerushalmi [forbids riding] — the reason is not because it suffers in his riding, only the reason is because of techumin.
